text:
ops-bot: ALERT: Multiple CUDA OOMs observed on gpu-node-14 (serving-runtime). Error spikes started ~10m ago. Auto-created thread.

samira (oncall): Seeing it. stack-trace in node logs points to failed `cudaMalloc` during kv-cache prefetch.

leo (eng-runtime): Can you paste the runtime diagnostic output? I want reserve/headroom numbers.

maya (sre): nvidia-smi snapshot from node attached below. Node is at 82% mem utilization across other pods, but runtime reports ~3.1Gi headroom.

samira (oncall): `kubectl logs -n inference runtime-pod-7 -c runtime | tail -n 50`
```
2026-03-15T09:02:23Z runtime INFO reserve=2048Mi reported_headroom=3170Mi kv_prefetch=enabled
2026-03-15T09:02:23Z runtime ERROR cudaMalloc(1600000000) failed: out of memory
2026-03-15T09:02:23Z runtime WARN attempted_alloc=1526Mi available_reported=3134Mi fragmentation_est=0.6
```

leo (eng-runtime): That fragmentation_est looks high. Reported available is > allocation, but allocator probably can't find a contiguous block due to reserved fragments + pinned spare.

ben (infra): `kubectl describe node gpu-node-14` shows some daemonsets using pinned memory (profilers). Also we have a small sparepool reserved for prewarm (200Mi).

samira (oncall): Quick mitigation suggestion: disable kv prefetch on the node and recycle the worst pods. We can set env override on the deployment to `KV_PREFETCH=0` and rollout.

leo (eng-runtime): Agreed. Also let's cordon the node for controlled evacuation while we drain the most memory-hungry pods.

maya (sre): Taking actions now.

infra-oncall: Running commands: `kubectl cordon gpu-node-14` -> done.

infra-oncall: `kubectl get pods -o wide --field-selector spec.nodeName=gpu-node-14 -n inference` shows these top mem pods: runtime-pod-7, batch-prefetch-3, analytics-agent-1.

samira (oncall): Start with rollout patch for runtime to disable prefetch for Canary. `kubectl set env deployment/runtime DEPLOY_OVERRIDE=kv_prefetch:0 -n inference` (will do canary 10%).

deploy-bot: Deploy started for deployment/runtime at commit b1f8d3. Canary 10% -> in progress.

samira (oncall): Also killing batch-prefetch-3 to free immediate memory. `kubectl delete pod batch-prefetch-3 -n inference`

leo (eng-runtime): After that, check `dmesg` for cuda errors and `journalctl -u kubelet` for OOM kill events. If allocator is returning high fragmentation, we should add a temporary de-fragmentation: restart runtime with `--evict-spare=true` but that's riskier. Let's avoid node-wide restarts unless needed.

maya (sre): batch-prefetch-3 deleted, pod came back on gpu-node-16. Memory freed on gpu-node-14 ~1.8Gi.

samira (oncall): Canary patch rolled up to 10% and canary pods on other nodes look fine. But we still see 2 more OOM trace entries.

leo (eng-runtime): Pasted a short allocator trace from runtime log: 
```
[alloc] try_alloc 1600000000 at 0x0
[alloc] free_segments: 4 segments (sizes: 512Mi, 256Mi, 1.1Gi, 128Mi)
[alloc] failed_contiguous_alloc -> fragmentation
[alloc] fallback: reserve_reclaim -> evict_kv_cache(1)
[alloc] cudaMalloc failed after reclaim
```

leo (eng-runtime): The allocator's fallback reclaim triggered eviction of small cache entries but the biggest contiguous segment (1.1Gi) was used by a pinned tensor from a different containerable slab; combined fragmentation prevented satisfying 1.6Gi. Reported headroom ignores reserved/pinned fragmentation.

ben (infra): We have a pinned profiler container grabbing 1.2Gi on that node (infra diagnostic). It's scheduled by monitoring. We can temporarily scale that DaemonSet down on this node.

maya (sre): Scaling monitoring daemonset to 0 on gpu-node-14: `kubectl scale ds/monitor-profiles -n infra --replicas=0 --field-selector=spec.nodeName=gpu-node-14` - note: `kubectl scale` doesn't support field-selector, doing a targeted eviction instead. Will delete specific pod.

ben (infra): Deleted monitor-profiles-gpu-14. Freed 1.2Gi. Observed immediate drop in fragmentation metric.

samira (oncall): After that, OOM events stopped. Latency improved. Marking as mitigated for immediate customer impact.

priya (customer-success): Customer C saw elevated 5xx rates starting 09:02. How many requests failed?

maya (sre): Looking at ingress logs: ~2300 failed token requests / 10m window, peak 12% error rate for tier-1 customers. We rerouted some traffic as part of failover, but some requests hit the affected node before pods were rescheduled.

priya (customer-success): I'll prepare a brief: impacted customers list + timeline + mitigations and share in customer channel.

leo (eng-runtime): Root cause writeup (short): allocator's headroom metric is an aggregated free memory number that doesn't account for non-contiguous pinned allocations (daemonsets and profiler). The runtime assumed contiguous availability. When a large allocation needed contiguous chunk >=1.5Gi, fragmentation prevented allocation and cudaMalloc failed even though reported_headroom > needed.

samira (oncall): Action items (short):
- (P0) Add an immediate alert: fragmentation_ratio > 0.5 && reported_headroom < requested_large_alloc -> fire OOM-warning (maya)
- (P1) Adjust reported headroom calculation to subtract pinned/reserved contiguous windows (leo)
- (P1) Make kv-cache prefetch conservative for allocations > 512Mi (leo)
- (P2) infra: prevent non-essential pinned pods on GPU serving nodes or pin them to separate GPU class (ben)
- (P2) instrument per-node contiguous-free histogram metric (trial) (leo/maya)

maya (sre): Filing an incident ticket with timeline and logs. Assigning follow-ups: infra/ben to adjust daemonset placement; runtime/leo to push patch for headroom calc.

infra-oncall: Node remains cordoned. We will uncordon after we confirm no regressions for 30m.

samira (oncall): Marking as mitigated -> no active OOMs for last 6m. Closing immediate incident thread but keeping postmortem and follow-ups live.

ops-bot: Incident P3-2026-0315-oom-frag created. Postmortem template assigned to samira (oncall).

priya (customer-success): I posted the customer-facing status update to #customers-impacted and notified top-tier customers.

leo (eng-runtime): Quick note: will open PR to change headroom calc and add contiguous-free metric + unit tests. PR ID will be linked in postmortem.

samira (oncall): Thanks everyone. Adding one more: consider small defrag periodic restart window for runtime to reduce long-lived fragmentation. Not immediate, but discuss in next infra sync. :white_check_mark:

(emoji reactions and short acknowledgements followed).
